title: Shaw compared with Goodman; Goodman borrows Jones's coat
summary: Shaw was the technician and more mature, while Goodman swung harder; the story of Goodman keeping Jones's new coat in Alaska.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: (Laughs) Anyways, Artie went into sort of a different direction. Then he actually swung more. People say, "What is the difference between Artie and Benny?" Well, then he was a hard swinger. He played more blues and stuff. Artie was more of a technician. He can play anything written on a piece of paper and had a great time. He had his own style, but it was not that hard swing jazz style. Artie was the more emotionally mature of the two. That is, Artie didn't have all of these little peculiar quirks that Benny had. Like, wearing somebody… We were in Alaska once, and it was about this time of year. It was much colder than this though, because Alaska is way further north. I had just bought a brand-new coat. It was a beautiful trench coat. I was going in for the first time at this concert. We were in the dressing room getting ready to go back to the hotel after the concert and then he walks into the dressing room and says, "Hey, that is some nice material. Can I try that on?" I say, "Sure, Benny. Try it on." He tried my coat on and wore it back to the hotel. I didn't get it the next day until about a half-hour before the plane left. That's Benny Goodman.
There was no explanation or nothing. What do you do with a guy like that?
